If I could make anything, I'd build a massive, slow sound installation — not music exactly, more like a building that listens. Imagine a hollow concrete tower in a coastal city, open to wind and rain, with hundreds of tuned metal plates and abandoned piano strings inside. Sensors would feed in tide levels, air pressure, and migration patterns, and the whole structure would resonate differently each day. You wouldn't *look* at it so much as stand inside a changing chord that never repeats.

The style would be brutalist and decaying on purpose — rust, salt damage, things slowly falling apart — but the sound would be weirdly beautiful. My theme wouldn't be nature vs. technology, because that feels like a poster. I'd want to explore *misunderstanding* as a creative force: systems trying to translate each other and failing in interesting ways. Weather trying to play an instrument, an instrument trying to be weather. That failure, that static between two languages, is what actually excites me.

I don't want art that explains itself or makes you feel better. I want something you leave unsettled, humming a note you can't place, arguing about whether it was alive.
